groups.name: Construct design / DNA synthesis
groups.purpose: A robotic pipette dispenses into a multiwell plate. A PCR thermocycler supports amplification and assembly of purchased DNA fragments.

items.name: DNA fragments, vector and enzymes
items.use: DNA fragments encode candidate sequences. Assembly and PCR reagents create or amplify the chosen construct. The slide does not imply PCR replaces commercial de novo DNA synthesis.
items.examples: Twist, GenScript, Tsingke; Vazyme for enzymes and cloning reagents

items.name: Liquid handling + thermocycler
items.use: The arm and dispenser represent automated transfer into wells; the PCR instrument controls temperature cycling. These are distinct tools in the same construction scene.
items.examples: Tecan, Hamilton; Thermo Fisher, Bio-Rad for thermocyclers

items.name: Multiwell plate, tips and tubes
items.use: Wells hold reactions; compatible tips and tubes support transfers and sample handling. Consumable format depends on the workflow.

groups.name: Protein expression & purification
groups.purpose: Culture cells express the protein. Chromatography separates it from the mixture; LC-MS is a subsequent analytical QC option.

items.name: Culture flask + medium
items.use: The flask, cell dots and medium bottle represent expression in an appropriate host. Protein yield is measured here, not created by a later assay.
items.examples: GenScript; Gibco / Thermo Fisher, OPM, Duoning for culture inputs

items.name: Chromatography column + resin
items.use: The bead-filled column represents chromatographic separation. A collected fraction contains the selected protein; resin and column chemistry depend on the sample.

items.name: LC-MS instrument
items.use: LC-MS can support identity and other analytical checks after preparation. It is not shown as the device performing preparative protein purification.

groups.name: Primary binding screen
groups.purpose: Combine target protein with antibody candidates, then read binding signals using the assay format appropriate to the program.

items.name: Y-shaped antibody + green target
items.use: The Y shape represents an antibody and the green cluster represents a recombinant target protein. These are schematic molecules, not structural models.

items.name: Binding platform + response curve
items.use: The instrument labeled BLI represents biolayer interferometry. SPR is another binding technology with different hardware. Kinetic parameters may share the same experiment and fit.
items.examples: Sartorius for BLI; Cytiva for Biacore SPR

items.name: Assay plate + sensors
items.use: Plates hold samples and BLI sensors or SPR chips provide the appropriate assay surface. A plate-based optical screen can be an alternative initial assay.
items.examples: JET Biofil / Corning for plates; Sartorius / Cytiva for platform-specific consumables

groups.name: Multi-property characterization
groups.purpose: Use complementary measurements to build linked evidence on binding, stability and developability. No single instrument measures every attribute.

items.name: SEC column + LC-MS + peak
items.use: The column and instrument represent analytical separation and mass-based analysis. SEC may assess size-related heterogeneity; LC-MS supports other compositional and identity questions.
items.examples: Waters, Agilent, Thermo Fisher; NanoMicro and Sepax for separation media / columns

items.name: Sample tube + thermometer + melt curve
items.use: A thermal assay measures a temperature-dependent signal. A melting transition is one stability readout; aggregation and formulation behavior need appropriate additional measurements.

items.name: Association / dissociation curve
items.use: The schematic curve represents a kinetic response. KD, kon and koff are related; shared assay context is needed to interpret and train on them.

groups.name: Cell-function validation
groups.purpose: Dose a relevant cell model and measure the chosen biological response. Potency is specific to the assay and does not establish clinical efficacy.

items.name: Pipette + cells + media
items.use: The pipette delivers candidate or assay reagent to cultured cells. Culture media, cytokines and reporter reagents depend on the model.
items.examples: Gibco / Thermo Fisher, Bio-Techne, Vazyme; Corning and JET Biofil for cultureware

items.name: Flow cytometer + dot plot
items.use: Cells pass through a flow cell and are measured individually. The diagram shows a laser crossing the channel and a schematic data plot.
items.examples: Waters Biosciences (formerly BD Biosciences); other flow-cytometry suppliers

items.name: Microscope / cell imaging
items.use: Imaging measures selected cellular features and responses. It is a complementary assay route rather than a mandatory sequential step after flow cytometry.

groups.name: Data integration & feedback
groups.purpose: Link sample identity, assay conditions and results so data can be reused in the next model-guided design cycle.

items.name: Plate records → database
items.use: The plate represents sample-indexed results and the cylinder represents stored, linked experimental records. Conditions and QC matter alongside the measured values.

items.name: Laptop + model graph
items.use: The node graph represents model-assisted analysis or design. It does not imply autonomous recursive improvement has been demonstrated.
items.examples: Genedata and connected analysis environments; model developers vary

items.name: Next design + return arrow
items.use: The feedback arrow returns evidence to construct selection. Automation and data orchestration support all six stages, not just the final card.
items.examples: Tecan, Hamilton; Benchling and Genedata for linked data workflows
